notes: 2026-09-21 update: Cadillac Australia's BEV lineup has expanded from a single model (Lyriq) to four - Optiq, Lyriq, Vistiq and the newly launched Lyriq-V - after the cadillac.com.au page kept returning crawl failures on the earlier fetch. Optiq and Vistiq are AU/NZ-market right-hand-drive models confirmed for 2026 (single-grade lineups: Optiq Sport AWD, Vistiq Platinum AWD 6-seat), corroborated consistently across CarExpert, Drive, GoAuto, RACV, thebeep.com.au and Man of Many. Lyriq-V launched 18 Sept 2026 (GoAuto, CarExpert) as Cadillac's first V-Series model in Australia, alongside a resolved price for the base Lyriq range (previously null here due to conflicting launch-era vs later pricing) - Lyriq Sport and Luxury are now both $90,000 before on-road costs / ~$95,000 drive-away, mechanically identical, differing only in trim. Lyriq/Lyriq-V battery is corrected to the AU-market-specific 92kWh usable pack (130kW DC / 22kW AC) rather than the US-market 102kWh/190kW figures previously recorded here in error - Cadillac AU fits smaller packs than the US domestic market across its whole EV range (also seen in Optiq 75kWh vs US and Vistiq 91kWh vs US 102kWh). Lyriq powerKw/torqueNm/zeroTo100s remain flagged low-confidence: CarExpert's Lyriq-V comparison piece states 384kW/720Nm/4.9s for Sport, but an earlier CarExpert price-cut article states 388kW/610Nm for the same car - not reconciled, so both are treated as uncertain even though a value is recorded. V2L (vehicle-to-load, a portable AC outlet) is not confirmed as built into any current Cadillac EV; GM instead sells V2H (vehicle-to-home backup, different technology, dedicated hardware) as an accessory not confirmed as offered in Australia - v2l set to null rather than guessed for all four variants. Towing capacity not confirmed for the Australian-market (post RHD-conversion) rating of any of the four models - set to null.
